lead: >-
  Iguazu Falls in Argentina, Peru's high-altitude roads and El Peñón rock in Colombia demand different levels of physical effort. The stop in Uruguay, by contrast, is a short sightseeing excursion reached by ferry. We explain what the active parts of the extensive eight-country journey actually include, and what the four-country filter does not promise.
---

## Adventures in Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay: what the filter really means

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring the four principal countries named above and adventure among the thematic tags. The current [“8 Countries of South America in 32 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also covers Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. **This is a selection based on countries that intersect within a longer itinerary, not a separate ready-made tour exclusively through Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay.**

Adventure takes different forms throughout the trip: walking paths at the waterfalls, travel across high-altitude terrain and the natural scenery around Guatapé. However, **the two-day 4×4 jeep journey takes place in Bolivia**, which is not named in the current filter. It would be misleading to treat all four selected countries as equally prominent adventure destinations. To assess the actual physical demands, examine the [complete day-by-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Argentina: Iguazu and the contrast of city life

In [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), the itinerary includes a group excursion to the Argentine side of the waterfalls with a Russian-speaking guide. Viewing walkways and humid rainforest call for comfortable shoes and enough time to walk between viewpoints, but **a multi-day jungle trek is not included**. After the excursion, the group flies to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The following day is devoted to the city's neighborhoods and a tango show.

The transition from nature to city life matters when choosing a travel style. If you want more time walking forest trails, you will need to extend your stay at Iguazu; calling the itinerary an “adventure tour” does not add another day in the national park. The Argentine and Brazilian sides of the falls are visited separately, allowing for the border crossing and domestic flights.

## Uruguay: a ferry excursion without a sports program

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited on a day trip from Buenos Aires. Included are an early transfer to the port, a ferry crossing, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide and the return to Argentina. This is **a ferry crossing followed by a city walk**, not rafting, an expedition or a marine wildlife excursion. There is no overnight stay in Uruguay.

[Montevideo's Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) offer a worthwhile introduction to the capital. The included format is useful if you want to see another country within limited time. Hiking in Uruguay's natural areas would require a separate itinerary, different stops and extra nights.

For the full journey, allowing adequate time for the return ferry is essential: the following day involves a flight to Chile. If planning independently, check terminal arrival times, document requirements and a buffer for possible schedule changes.

## Peru: Titicaca and Machu Picchu without the Inca Trail

The Peru section follows the high-altitude portion of the journey through Bolivia. Travelers cross the border at Desaguadero, arrive in [Puno and at Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), visit the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) and take a tourist bus across the Andes to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). At this stage, the altitude, lengthy road journeys and opportunities to rest between excursions determine how demanding the trip feels.

A day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is included with an English-speaking guide. The return to Cusco is by train. **A multi-day hike along the Inca Trail is not part of the stated program**; the presence of Machu Picchu does not make such a trek an included activity. After sightseeing at Cusco's monuments, the group flies to Lima for a cultural tour of the capital.

For moderately active travelers, this section combines highland landscapes with guided visits. Anyone looking for a camping trek should compare specific [adventure itineraries featuring Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/) according to their actual hiking days and included services.

## Colombia: the Guatapé rock and the cities

From [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the 32-day itinerary includes an excursion to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) with an English-speaking guide. The rocky outcrop, hills and reservoir create the area's dramatic scenery. **Climbing the steps to the top is not explicitly stated as a mandatory included service**, so confirm the arrangements in advance if that is a priority.

The itinerary continues through [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) in Medellín, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). These are primarily excursions focusing on cities, monuments and architecture. The confirmed itinerary does not include mountaineering, rafting or multi-day hiking expeditions in Colombia.

The Colombian section therefore offers a balance of nature and urban culture. A dedicated Colombian adventure itinerary would require a separate program and changes to domestic flights.

## Why the eight-country tour cannot simply be reduced to four

The actual tour travels from Argentina to Uruguay and back to Argentina, then continues through Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Brazil comes at the start of the whole journey. Removing every country except the four in this page title changes the sequence of international flights and eliminates the Bolivian jeep section, which accounts for a substantial part of the full tour's adventurous character.

We help you define your priorities first — waterfalls, walks in the Andes, more demanding hiking or a variety of urban and natural experiences — and then agree on the route and pace of travel. Altitude in Peru and Bolivia, humidity at Iguazu and flights between distant regions all call for different packing choices and sensible rest periods. One adventure tag does not mean every day has the same physical difficulty.

For a geographical selection without a thematic filter, see [Argentina — Colombia — Peru — Uruguay](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru_uruguay/). If adventure is your main motivation, it is worth comparing [other multi-country adventure tours](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) and checking their specific activities.

## Frequently asked questions about adventure travel across four countries

### Is an Inca Trail hike included?

No. The current itinerary visits Machu Picchu with an English-speaking guide and returns to Cusco by train. A multi-day trek requires a separate program, permits and additional days.

### Can the ferry to Uruguay be considered an adventure excursion?

The ferry is transportation from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. The Uruguay program consists of sightseeing in the city and returning the same day, with no water sports or nature expedition.

### Where do the jeep journey and highest-altitude sections take place?

The two-day off-road trip among lagoons and salt flats takes place in Bolivia, after the stop in San Pedro de Atacama. It belongs to the complete eight-country route, although Bolivia is absent from the title of this four-country filter.

### Can I travel only through Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia?

A custom route covering those countries can be discussed. Flights, duration and excursions would need to be agreed afresh; the prices and conditions of the 32-day tour cannot automatically be applied to a shorter trip.

## From port capitals to Inca heritage and Colombian cities

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which **Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay** are principal countries, with culture and history among the key themes. Our catalogue features [“8 Countries of South America in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Beyond the four named countries, this itinerary includes Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. The countries in the title therefore form **a search selection within a larger program**, not a promise of a separate trip confined to them.

The cultural itinerary is a journey through different eras. Buenos Aires and Montevideo reveal the history of cities on the shores of the Río de la Plata; Peru introduces highland traditions and Inca monuments; and Colombia adds the Caribbean coast, art and the urban memory of Medellín and Bogotá. These experiences receive very different amounts of time, from a single ferry day to several consecutive stops in the Andes.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Argentina: historic neighborhoods and tango in the itinerary

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a three-hour group city tour with a Russian-speaking guide is included. The named stops include [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), [Recoleta](/argentina/place/recoleta/) and Puerto Madero. These neighborhoods illustrate how the port capital has changed, from historic urban streets to modern waterfront districts.

An evening tango show with dinner is also included. It is a substantial cultural experience, but **a separate tango lesson is not included**. Travelers who wish to learn the dance or explore museum collections should allow extra time. With long journeys between countries, it helps to decide in advance what matters most: an introductory walk, a stage performance or a deeper exploration of urban history.

The Argentine section begins after the excursion to Iguazu Falls. That visit belongs to the nature-focused part of the journey and does not replace a full cultural day in the capital.

## Uruguay: Montevideo between two nights in Argentina

The next day, travelers leave early for the port of Buenos Aires and cross the Río de la Plata by ferry. An excursion with an English-speaking guide and some free time are planned in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/); the group returns to Argentina that evening. **The itinerary does not include an overnight stay in Uruguay.**

[Montevideo's Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) and the [Metropolitan Cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/) introduce the historic spaces of Uruguay's capital. However, a day trip with transport connections leaves limited time for museums. If Uruguayan history is a primary interest, it is better to discuss additional nights rather than trying to fit extra visits in before the return ferry.

For a journey through four or more countries, this is also a matter of reliable logistics: the return to Buenos Aires connects with the onward flight to Chile. We help coordinate transfers and time buffers so that the day trip does not disrupt the next stages.

## Peru: from Lake Titicaca to Cusco and Machu Picchu

Peru offers the longest continuous historical and cultural section in this combination. After visiting Tiwanaku in **Bolivia**, travelers cross the border at Desaguadero and arrive in [Puno, at Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), known for their reed-building traditions, is planned here. The next day brings a tourist-bus journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with stops along the Andean route and lunch en route.

A separate excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) then takes place with an English-speaking guide; the travelers return to Cusco by train. This is a visit to an archaeological site, **not a multi-day Inca Trail trek**. In Cusco, the itinerary includes [Qorikancha](/peru/place/coricancha/), [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/), Qenqo, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay. Together, these sites show different aspects of religious and defensive architecture in the region.

The final Peruvian stop is [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), including Miraflores, [Plaza Mayor](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/) and colonial architecture. There is an alternative arrangement for the Cathedral: if it is closed, the excursion visits the MALI museum instead. This distinction matters, because it would be incorrect to promise both visits on the same day.

Peru also changes the demands of preparing for the trip. The altitude of Puno and Cusco, long mountain drives and busy sightseeing days call for time to acclimatize. You will benefit from keeping some energy in reserve even though the route focuses on history rather than sporting treks.

## Colombia: a fortified port, street art and museums

After Ecuador, which falls between Peru and Colombia in the complete itinerary, travelers arrive in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). One of the cultural highlights is [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), a neighborhood known for its recent urban history and artistic transformation. However, that day also includes a flight to Cartagena, so there is not enough free time for an in-depth exploration of every district of Medellín.

In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), a four-hour tour with a Russian-speaking guide is planned. The itinerary mentions views across the bay, historic quarters, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, San Pedro Claver Church and the Santo Domingo bastion. The port city and its fortifications are on the UNESCO World Heritage List. This is a different colonial story from that of Buenos Aires: Cartagena developed as a fortified Caribbean port.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the focus shifts to La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, Bolívar Square and [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/). The following day includes a visit to the [Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) with an English-speaking guide. This order offers two distinct cultural experiences: exploring museums in the capital and visiting an unusual religious site outside the city. Museum opening days need to be checked for the actual travel dates; closed exhibitions cannot be treated as guaranteed visits.

## What Peru adds to this thematic combination compared with Ecuador

In the [Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay combination](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_ecuador_uruguay/interests/culture-and-history/), Quito, its old-town architecture and the Equator line take center stage. **Here the added central theme is Peru's Inca monuments and highland culture:** Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

These are different filters for **the same extensive eight-country journey**. Peru and Ecuador do not replace one another in our tour; both are included. A custom four-country product would require choosing the country sequence afresh, allocating cultural days and confirming flights and cost. Comparing [multi-country cultural and historical journeys](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) also reveals other genuinely available combinations.

## Choosing the pace of a cultural itinerary

The main question is not the number of countries itself, but how many days remain for monuments and museums after travel. A day in Montevideo offers a first impression, but not a comprehensive exploration of the country. Peru receives several consecutive days, although some of that time goes on driving across the Andes and on flights. In Colombia, museum schedules and transfers between Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá are especially important.

Ada Tours helps you discuss priority cultural sites, guide languages, the need for extra museum days and sufficient time between connections. The [Argentina — Colombia — Peru — Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru_uruguay/) shows the full geographical selection without the thematic filter.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural travel across four countries

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Yes. The current 32-day tour includes a group excursion from Cusco to Machu Picchu with an English-speaking guide and a return journey by train.

### Is Tiwanaku in Peru?

No. The Tiwanaku archaeological complex is in **Bolivia**. The published itinerary visits it before crossing the border into Peru and reaching Puno. It should not be confused with Peru's own monuments.

### Can we spend several nights in Uruguay?

The ready-made itinerary visits Montevideo on a day trip from Buenos Aires. Extra nights can be discussed as a custom modification, with subsequent travel arrangements recalculated.

### Should I choose this combination or the one with Ecuador?

For the history of the Incas, the Peruvian days offer more: Cusco, Machu Picchu and Titicaca. Ecuador is important for Quito's historic architecture and the Equator line. The full eight-country journey includes both, while a shorter four-country trip needs separate planning.

## Nature travel in Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

This selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: [“8 Countries of South America in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Each of the four named countries has specific stops, but they are spread throughout a longer journey covering Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia.

The main natural contrasts within this combination are **Iguazu Falls, Peru's high-altitude geography and Colombia's rocky landscapes**. Travel and flights between them take time, and the Uruguay visit is one day focused on the city. When choosing an itinerary, the experiences in each stage therefore matter more than the number of countries in the title.

Tours featuring all four countries appear in the [general combination catalogue](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru_uruguay/), while other destinations can be compared in the [Nature section](/interests/nature/).

## Argentina: from the waterfalls to the capital

After Brazil's Foz do Iguaçu, the group explores the Argentine side of the falls near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Elevated walkways bring visitors close to the rushing water, including the route towards the [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/) when access is open.

This day differs from the distant panoramic views on the Brazilian shore: you experience the noise of the falls, the damp air and the tropical forest around them. The trails available on the day depend on conditions in the national park and water levels. The route is adjusted if necessary to comply with restrictions, so access to any particular viewing platform cannot be guaranteed in advance.

After Iguazu, travelers fly to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for cultural and city excursions. **Patagonia is not part of the Argentine section**: this tour should not be presented as a journey to all of Argentina's natural attractions.

## Uruguay: one day in Montevideo

On day nine, the itinerary includes a ferry trip from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Following sightseeing with an English-speaking guide, the group returns to Argentina. This is **not** a separate journey through Uruguay's natural parks: the stop centers on the capital and its urban culture.

It is a worthwhile stop for travelers who want to discover another country without a long additional overland journey. Nevertheless, it would be inaccurate to treat it as a nature day comparable to Iguazu or Lake Titicaca.

Because the ferry crosses an international border, the requirements for leaving and re-entering Argentina must be considered. Timetables and potential weather changes affect the day's arrangements.

## Peru: Titicaca, the Andean road and the mountains around Machu Picchu

Travelers reach the Peruvian portion after Chile and high-altitude Bolivia. The route includes the border crossing at Desaguadero, [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and a visit to the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The lake lies high in the Andes, a sharp contrast to the humid lowlands of Iguazu.

The group then travels from Puno to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) by tourist bus, with stops and lunch along the way. The mountain road itself, the changes in altitude and the length of the journey are important here. Travelers sensitive to altitude should consider this stage together with the preceding section in Bolivia. The eight-country journey reaches high elevations before entering Peru.

An excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) follows, with train travel and a guide. The archaeological site is surrounded by green mountains. Its setting is striking, but **the Machu Picchu day in this itinerary primarily visits the historic complex**, without a separate multi-day trek.

From Cusco, travelers fly to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) for an introductory city tour. The Peruvian portion therefore combines high-altitude scenery, ancient monuments and cities.

## Colombia: El Peñón, Guatapé and city panoramas

Towards the end of the journey, after Ecuador, the group arrives in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). One day is devoted to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The rock and reservoir landscape, with its many inlets, create a very different natural scene from the Peruvian highlands.

If you plan to climb the rock, consider the number of steps, current trail conditions and your fitness. Access arrangements and whether there is time for the ascent should be checked before the visit; including the site in the tour does not guarantee every participant a climb to the summit.

Afterwards, we arrange city tours of Medellín, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), including the [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/) area. Here, natural scenery meets urban life and culture. The tour does not advertise jungle safaris or lengthy hikes in Colombia's national parks.

## Comparing the natural experiences of the four countries

| Country | What you will see |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazu Falls |
| Uruguay | Urban Montevideo |
| Peru | Titicaca, the Andes and the scenery around Machu Picchu |
| Colombia | El Peñón and Guatapé |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Our full tour lasts **32 days and 31 nights**; the published departure dates are **22 October – 22 November 2026**. Availability for other departures must be checked separately: these dates do not establish future seat or flight availability.

Prices start from **$15,500 per person sharing a double room (½ DBL)**; single occupancy (SGL) is **$18,600**. The itinerary specifies 4-star hotels, domestic flights, excursions and transfers; international flights, additional activities and personal expenses are charged separately. The final amount is agreed according to the actual booking arrangements.

A route restricted to Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay would require different logistics. It is not possible simply to remove Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador from the complete tour and retain the same flights, prices and overnight sequence.

## Altitude, exertion, entry requirements and transport

The most significant natural challenge in this combination is **the altitude of the Peruvian Andes**. Moreover, travelers reach Puno after several high-altitude days in Bolivia. Acclimatization needs and individual tolerance for exertion should be considered before choosing travel dates and a route; medical restrictions call for an individual approach.

For Iguazu, bring protection against spray; for the Peruvian highlands, warm clothing and sun protection; and for walks in Colombia, comfortable shoes. On a 32-day trip involving several domestic flights, agree on baggage allowances in advance.

Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia, along with the other four countries, have their own entry and transit rules. Visa requirements depend on citizenship, passport documents and travel dates. Ada Tours helps coordinate transportation, local guides, flights and a checklist of requirements to verify against official sources, without guaranteeing visa issuance or admission across a border.

## Frequently asked questions about the itinerary

### Can I spend 32 days exclusively in these four countries?

The current itinerary covers eight countries. A four-country route requires separate planning and pricing.

### Does the Uruguay stop include a wildlife reserve or wild nature?

No. It is a one-day sightseeing trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo.

### Does Machu Picchu count as trekking on this itinerary?

No. The program specifies an excursion to the complex with train travel. A separate multi-day hike is not included.

### Which sections require particular attention to altitude?

The high-altitude parts of Bolivia and the subsequent stops in Puno and Cusco in Peru. These should be assessed together.

### Which is the shortest stop among these countries?

Uruguay takes one day, with a return to Buenos Aires in the evening; the other selected countries have longer stays.

## Where to watch wildlife on a route through Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay among the main countries. It features the [“8 Countries of South America in 32 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). All four selected countries are on that route, but the complete journey also passes through Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador.

**Argentina's most substantial nature stop is [Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/)**. In Peru, the itinerary reaches high-altitude Lake Titicaca and crosses the Andes; in Colombia, it explores the landscapes around [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The day in Uruguay centers on [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), rather than a safari or nature reserve.

The main organized island-wildlife experience is in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador. It is included in the full itinerary even though Ecuador is absent from the name of this four-country filter. Nature lovers should examine **the entire current tour and how its nature-focused days are distributed**, rather than assume there are wildlife excursions in each selected country.

## Argentina: forests, waterfalls and wildlife without guarantees

The Argentine nature section follows sightseeing trails near Iguazu Falls. You enter an area of subtropical forest, with walkways offering views of the cascades and gorge from different perspectives. The program visits both sides of the falls, but the Argentine and Brazilian sides are separate stops involving their own transfers.

The park protects habitats for many birds and mammals. Toucans, coatis, monkeys and other species live here, but the presence of an animal on a protected-species list **does not guarantee a sighting during a particular walk**. On the Ada Tours program, this is a guided waterfall excursion, not specialist birdwatching or a search for jaguars.

The experience at Iguazu contrasts neatly with the later [city day in Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/): on the next stage, nature trails give way to neighborhoods, historic architecture and tango. Travelers wishing to spend more time with Argentina's nature can explore [nature tours in Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) separately.

## Peru: mountain scenery, Titicaca and Inca heritage

The Peruvian part of the full journey begins with travel from Bolivia to Puno and an excursion to the Uros Islands on Lake Titicaca. A tourist-bus journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) follows, along with a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and guided tours of the region's monuments.

This is a combination of high-altitude geography and culture. The lake, mountain passes, valleys and terraces create memorable natural impressions, but **our itinerary makes no separate promise of rare-animal watching in Peru**. The Machu Picchu visit is organized as a train excursion with a return to Cusco, not a multi-day trek through mountain reserves.

Altitude affects wellbeing, weather and walking pace. For the Peruvian days, assess your personal tolerance of altitude and bring clothing for cool mornings, even if you have previously been in hotter regions. A more focused choice is available in the [Peru nature-tour catalogue](/interests/nature/tours/peru/), although the precise activities should be checked against each trip's itinerary.

## Colombia and Uruguay: what they contribute to the nature theme

In Colombia, travelers visit [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and the El Peñón area before exploring Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. The rock, hills and reservoir are the attractions of the Guatapé excursion, but it is **a scenic outing**, with no advertised program for observing wild animals. The following days' city tours focus instead on history and culture.

In Uruguay, the itinerary includes a ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), a guided walk and a return to Argentina on the same day. The sea crossing is transportation to the capital; it is not described as a cruise for watching whales or birds.

These four countries thus offer different experiences: waterfalls and forest, Andean landscapes, a scenic reservoir and a city on an estuary. If wildlife encounters are the main reason for your trip, it is especially helpful to compare these stages with the Ecuador section of the full journey.

## Why the Galápagos change the choice of the full itinerary

In Ecuador, the itinerary allocates time to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/): a flight to Baltra, transfer to Santa Cruz, the island's highlands and a day of marine excursions. On this section, you may observe giant tortoises and island birds in the relevant locations on the program.

**The marine excursion has alternatives:** North Seymour and Bachas Beach **or** South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The actual option is confirmed after booking. Both branches are not promised together, and the species observed depend on the chosen island and natural conditions.

For a trip centered on wildlife, consider the length of the island stay, excursion format and confirmed option. If you want to combine nature with the history of capitals, Peruvian monuments and Colombia, the wider 32-day route serves a different purpose. See also [multi-country wildlife-watching journeys](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

## Travel arrangements and confirming conditions

The full journey combines flights, overland transfers and the Buenos Aires–Montevideo ferry. It alternates between humid subtropical areas, mountains, Pacific islands and major cities. Packing from a single “South America” weather chart makes little sense: prepare for wet walks, high altitudes and sea crossings.

We help coordinate the order of stops, transfers and guides and check entry requirements in advance **for all eight countries on the actual itinerary**, taking travelers' citizenship into account. At the time of booking, the rules for visiting protected areas and the selected sea excursion are also confirmed. A custom itinerary can include discussions about adding more nature days, but these additions should not be treated as part of the ready-made product.

For tours of any theme featuring these countries, use the [general Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru_uruguay/). This page specifically addresses nature and wildlife within the current itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about the nature itinerary

### Can I see wild animals in all four countries?

No. The current tour does not include specialist wildlife watching in every country. Argentina offers the Iguazu nature park; Peru and Colombia mainly offer scenery and cultural excursions; and Uruguay offers an introduction to the capital. The most substantial island-wildlife section is in Ecuador.

### Is the Galápagos excursion part of this selection?

It is part of the full [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), which is also shown here. The Galápagos themselves, however, are in Ecuador, outside the four countries named in the filter.

### Can a jaguar or particular bird sighting be guaranteed?

No. Even protected areas rich in wildlife cannot guarantee that a given species will appear on a visitor trail. If you want to observe a specific animal, choose a dedicated format and check its itinerary.

### Do I need to prepare for altitude if my main interest is nature?

Yes. The full route includes Andean regions in Bolivia and Peru. Alongside comfortable footwear and sun protection, assess altitude risks, the sequence of overnight stays and your own medical restrictions.

## Why Argentina and Uruguay make a natural pair, while Colombia needs a separate stage

[Argentina](/argentina/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) form a natural pairing around the Río de la Plata estuary. From [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), you can cross to the other shore for a day in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Although it involves an international border, this excursion feels like part of a single South American city itinerary.

[Colombia](/colombia/) is much farther north. It adds a variety that a journey between the capitals on the Río de la Plata cannot provide: [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) is surrounded by mountains, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) faces the Caribbean Sea, and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) lies high in the Andes. Traveling between these places requires dedicated transport days and a carefully planned flight sequence.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include Argentina, Uruguay and Colombia on their principal routes. The currently confirmed ready-made itinerary is the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). In addition to these three countries, it passes through Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. The title of this selection identifies a combination within an existing longer tour; **a separate ready-made itinerary limited to exactly these three countries is not advertised here**.

## Montevideo from Buenos Aires: returning to Argentina matters

The published tour follows a specific sequence: first the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, then a sightseeing tour of Buenos Aires and an evening of tango. The next day is devoted to Uruguay. An early transfer to the port, **a ferry to Montevideo**, a guided tour with an English-speaking guide, free time and a return to Buenos Aires are included. Ferry tickets form part of the stated itinerary. No overnight stay in Uruguay is planned in this version.

On a round trip completed in one day, consider more than the ferry's sailing time: check-in, passport control, time at the port and weather on the water also matter. A crucial detail is that after visiting Montevideo, travelers **re-enter Argentina**. Entry conditions must therefore be checked for the entire sequence of border crossings, not just arrival at the start of the journey. Requirements for holders of passports from other countries may differ from those for Russian citizens.

If you want a leisurely exploration of [Montevideo's Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), walks on the waterfront and more places around Uruguay, a different timetable is needed. A one-day visit is suited to a first acquaintance with the capital; several nights change both transport costs and the overall duration. You can see current offers including the country in the [Uruguay tour catalogue](/uruguay/tour/), but each program's exact contents need to be checked.

## How Colombia appears in the larger itinerary

After the return from Uruguay, the ready-made route continues through Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. Only then does the Colombian section begin: a flight from Guayaquil to Medellín, an excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), sightseeing in Medellín, a flight to Cartagena, then Bogotá and Zipaquirá. Colombia is therefore not the next stop immediately after the ferry to Montevideo.

| Section | What makes it distinctive |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires – Montevideo | Ferry crossing, two border procedures and return to Argentina |
| Southern countries – Colombia | A long sequence of countries and flights |
| Within Colombia | Cities at different elevations and the Caribbean coast |

For a custom trip limited to these three countries, it is more convenient to plan Argentina and Uruguay as one southern stage, with Colombia as the second. You will need to agree on travel between the stages, the Colombian airport of arrival and the return flight. We help arrange the city sequence, transfers and sensible buffers between flights. The precise route depends on available tickets and the group's preferences; the name of this selection does not promise a direct flight between the cities concerned.

## Visas and documents: what has been verified for Russian citizens

According to official consular information checked on **16 October 2026**, Russian citizens with valid ordinary international passports can visit Argentina, Uruguay and Colombia visa-free for tourism for **up to 90 days in each 180-day period** in the respective country. Stay limits are calculated under each country's own rules, not as a single allowance shared among the three.

For a trip from Argentina to Montevideo and back, it is particularly important to confirm that the passport and itinerary allow re-entry into Argentina and that all personal requirements are met. Consular guidance for Colombia also calls for verification of passport validity. In addition to visa rules, travelers should prepare evidence of onward travel, necessary bookings and documents for children where relevant.

If the route connects through an airport in a different country, also establish whether immigration clearance is required to collect baggage or change terminals. Visa-free access to Argentina, Uruguay and Colombia for Russians **does not override** transit rules in an intermediate country. Travelers taking the published eight-country journey need their documents checked for the entire route.

## Three different pesos and how to pay

The names of the currencies are deceptively similar: the Argentine peso, Uruguayan peso and Colombian peso are **three different currencies**. Cash left over from Buenos Aires does not become local currency in Montevideo or Bogotá. For a short ferry visit, it is especially useful to determine in advance which expenses are already paid and how much local cash will actually be needed.

US dollars may sometimes be used in currency exchanges or certain tourist transactions, but you cannot expect to pay everywhere using dollar banknotes. Local payment methods apply to groceries, city transport and small services. Exchange rates, fees and the ability to pay a specific merchant should be checked closer to departure.

Visa cards issued by Russian banks **are not serviced outside Russia by the international Visa network**; travelers cannot rely on a Russian-bank Mastercard abroad either. For a card from a foreign bank, check where it works, cash-withdrawal options and fees. We help distinguish prepaid services from expenses payable locally, but travelers should not assume that currency exchange, a foreign bank card or other financial services will necessarily be provided.

## Southern spring, the Caribbean and the mountains: what to pack

In October and November, Buenos Aires and Montevideo are in the Southern Hemisphere's spring. Ocean breezes and changeable weather around the Río de la Plata make a light windproof jacket useful even when daytime temperatures are pleasant. Colombia is different: Cartagena's coast is hot and humid, while Bogotá stands more than 2,500 m above sea level and is usually much cooler. Climatic contrasts can be striking even on a single day of travel.

For the southern city section, bring comfortable shoes, wind protection and a small kit for the ferry. Add lightweight clothing for hot weather, sun protection and rainwear for Colombia. Two entirely separate sets of shoes are not essential; being able to adjust clothing layers quickly and avoid overloading luggage matters more. Check luggage arrangements for the ferry and short flights with the chosen carriers.

For travel insurance, check coverage in all three territories, planned activities and medical assistance conditions. Medical recommendations, including possible yellow-fever vaccination, depend on the Colombian regions visited, travel through other countries and individual health. Such a vaccination should not be declared mandatory for every visit to Bogotá or Cartagena without checking the specific itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I visit Uruguay from Buenos Aires without staying overnight?

Yes. On the current eight-country tour, this is a one-day outing: an early ferry to Montevideo, sightseeing, free time and a return to the Argentine capital. Ferry tickets are included in the stated itinerary. Sailing times are checked before booking.

### Does a Russian citizen need a visa for a one-day visit to Uruguay?

Tourist entry on an ordinary Russian international passport is visa-free. Travelers must also check their right to re-enter Argentina, their documents and the carrier's conditions.

### Why can't Colombia simply be added to the ferry excursion?

It lies in a different part of the continent. Getting to Medellín, Cartagena or Bogotá requires a separate transport sequence. In the ready-made tour, travelers pass through Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador before reaching Colombia.

### Can Argentine pesos be used in Uruguay and Colombia?

These are different national currencies. Even where a merchant voluntarily accepts foreign money, the rate and conditions may be unfavorable. It is better to budget local expenses separately for each stage.

### What season is best for these countries?

Compare weather by city rather than countrywide averages: springtime Buenos Aires and Montevideo, cool Bogotá and hot Cartagena require different clothing. Travel dates depend on your preferred excursions and the ferry and flight schedules.
